title: Neural Conductor: Animate ShaderBalls with BrainStem Poses
description: A BrainStem character stands at the center of a circular arena surrounded by 5 orbiting ShaderBalls. The user controls the BrainStem's animation playback and uses it to 'conduct' the ShaderBalls — each pose keyframe triggers different animation behaviors on the ShaderBalls including pulsing scale, color shifts, orbit speed changes, and vertical bobbing. Users must hit specific pose-to-effect combinations to complete a choreography sequence.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads BrainStem.glb centered at the origin and 5 instances of ShaderBall.glb arranged in a circle (radius 4) around it. Setup: Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4), a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.2, and a subtle hemisphere light. Use a dark gradient background (0x1a1a2e). Add OrbitControls with damping. Animation System: Parse all AnimationClips from BrainStem. Create a GUI panel (HTML overlay, not dat.gui) with: (1) a dropdown to select animation clip, (2) a play/pause toggle button, (3) a speed slider from 0.1x to 3.0x, (4) a 'timeScale' slider that maps the current animation time normalized (0-1) to ShaderBall effects. ShaderBall Behaviors: Each ShaderBall responds to the BrainStem animation progress differently — Ball 1 scales between 0.5 and 1.5 based on animation progress, Ball 2 changes its Y position (bobbing 0 to 2 units), Ball 3 changes orbit speed (0.2 to 4.0 rad/s), Ball 4 rotates on its local X-axis proportional to playback speed, Ball 5 has its emissive material color lerp from blue to red based on progress. Add a 'Choreography Mode' button that displays a sequence of 6 target states (e.g., 'Set clip to Walk, speed 2x, progress > 0.7'). The user must match each target by adjusting controls. Validate each step: check clip name, speed range (within 0.2 tolerance), and normalized time (within 0.1 tolerance). Show a progress tracker (Step 1/6 ... 6/6) and a success banner with confetti-like particle burst on completion. Display real-time debug info: current clip name, normalized time, playback speed. All ShaderBall materials should be set to MeshStandardMaterial with metalness 0.8 and roughness 0.2 for visual appeal. Add a subtle ground plane with grid helper.
